# Couchbird

> An IPTV player for Fire TV, Android TV, Google TV and NVIDIA Shield. It plays your own provider's Xtream Codes or M3U playlist: a sports guide matched to your channels, local channels first, recording, multi-view, no ads or trackers. It does not provide any content.

## Couchbird at a glance
- What it is: an IPTV player app for Fire TV, Android TV, Google TV and NVIDIA Shield.
- What it isn't: a TV service. It includes no channels, films or shows. Users sign in with their own provider's Xtream Codes login or M3U playlist.
- Status: not released yet. Coming to Google Play and the Amazon Appstore.
- Price at launch: free for 7 days, then $5.99 a year or $19.99 once.
- Built for: live sports matched to the user's channels, local news first, a full TV guide, recording, catch-up, and two or four channels at once.
- Privacy: no ads, no analytics, no trackers and no account. The provider login stays encrypted on the TV.
- Devices: Fire TV Stick (2nd gen or newer), Fire TV Cube, NVIDIA Shield, Chromecast with Google TV, Google TV Streamer and Android TV 7.1 or newer. Not Roku, Apple TV, or Samsung and LG TVs' own systems.
- Contact: support@couchbird.app
